before: blockquote marks a quoted block; q marks a short quotation within a sentence. Markup describes that relationship, not whether the quotation is accurate or legally reusable. The words in this lesson were invented for this exercise, not taken from a publication.

The cite attribute can store a source URL. Browsers do not ordinarily turn that attribute into a visible source label. A cite element, which is different from the attribute, marks the title of a work. Put readable attribution in ordinary page content when readers need it.

This fragment shows a block quotation and a separate source description. ```html

Leave the path clearer than you found it.

From Trail volunteer notes, an invented example.

``` The URL is metadata on blockquote. Trail volunteer notes remains visible inside cite. Merely changing the URL would not rewrite those visible words. For a short inline quote, use a q element in a sentence, for example

The invented note says Leave a clear path.

. A browser normally supplies quotation punctuation for q; do not add a second pair merely to imitate its default appearance.

Mark the invented notebook statement as a block quotation. Store its source URL and display Notebook practice as the work title outside the quote. A parser can verify these separate roles, not the truth or permission status of a real quotation.
after: A quote repeats someone’s exact words. Put a quote that stands on its own inside `<blockquote>`. This lesson uses made-up words so you can practise the HTML.
The `cite` attribute on `<blockquote>` stores a source address. It does not show that address on the page. Write the source below the quote so readers can see it.

Here is a quote with a visible source. ```html

Leave the path clearer than you found it.

From Trail volunteer notes, an invented example.

``` `
` holds the quoted words. Its `cite` attribute stores the address. The paragraph below shows the source. Inside that paragraph, `` marks the title of the work: Trail volunteer notes.

Put the starter sentence inside `<blockquote>`. Set its `cite` attribute to `https://example.org/journal`. Below the quote, add a paragraph that says `Source:` and put `Notebook practice` inside `<cite>`. The title must stay outside the quote.

before.question: You add cite="https://example.org/journal" to blockquote but add no visible source text. Does that attribute itself display an attribution line?
choices: Yes. It automatically prints the URL below the quote.
Only when the URL ends in journal.
before.explanation: The cite attribute stores a source address; it is not ordinary rendered attribution text.

after.question: You add a cite address to a blockquote. Does that show the source below the quote?
choices: Yes, the browser prints the address.
No. You need to write a visible source line.
Only if the address ends in journal.
after.explanation: The attribute stores the address. A separate paragraph lets readers see the source.
